function_lacks_delegatecall_guard.meaning: injectSweepAndCall is a normal external function with no onlyDelegatecall or equivalent restriction

called_directly_on_router.meaning: injectSweepAndCall is invoked directly on the router contract rather than via delegatecall from a wallet/shim

user_funds_sent_to_router.meaning: a user sends funds to the router expecting stateless routing behavior

target_misconfigured_or_fails.meaning: the target of the injected call is misconfigured, malicious, or fails

router_balance_drained_by_attacker.meaning: an attacker withdraws/drains the accumulated token balances held by the router

claims.scope: injectSweepAndCall on TrailsRouter called directly instead of via delegatecall

preconditions.text: injectSweepAndCall is declared as a normal external function without any onlyDelegatecall or equivalent restriction.; injectSweepAndCall is called directly on the router contract rather than via delegatecall from a wallet/shim.; A user sends funds to the router expecting stateless routing behavior.; The target of the injected call is misconfigured, malicious, or fails.
preconditions.derivation: Program conjunction of selected report preconditions.

safety.text: injectSweepAndCall should only execute in a delegatecall context where address(this) is the user's wallet/shim, so the router never accumulates or controls user funds.
safety.derivation: Program synthesis from the selected intent and logical pattern.

effects.text: Via the previously reported missing delegatecall guard bug, anyone can withdraw tokens from the router and an attacker can drain these accumulated balances.
effects.derivation: Program-generated direct negation witness for the selected safety pattern.

effect_coverage.reason: Program-generated exact coverage for selected direct impact.

assumptions: The router holds accumulated user funds at the time of the direct call, as implied by the drain impact.
The 'anyone can withdraw' capability comes from a separate previously reported bug not detailed in this report.

limitations: Scenario is conditional/potential; no concrete transaction, amounts, tokens, or target configuration are given.
The drain relation is represented as a grounded Boolean because the report gives no numeric amounts or withdrawal formula.
The target-misconfiguration precondition is not part of the drain condition; it supports the separate stuck-funds impact handled in another pass.
